title: Novel methodologies to minimize pediatric PET/CT dose
text:
The proposed research has significant and important implications for use of PET/CT in pediatric patients.
The targeted radiation dose reduction and scan time shortening will increase safety and simplify workflows
around PET/CT, resulting in immediate impacts on clinical use and paving the way for future impacts in terms
of increasing the use of this powerful modality in research and clinical care. Our work will markedly decrease
patient radiation exposure and the need for sedation or anesthesia for children who benefit from the unique
information provided by PET/CT.

title: Continued Development of Infant Neuroimaging Analysis Tools
text:
This project is dedicated to 1) creating and disseminating the first set of multi-site applicable, infant cerebellum-
dedicated neuroimage analysis tools based on cutting-edge deep learning techniques to enable precise
quantification of early cerebellum development, and also 2) adding new cerebrum-related functionalities and
improving existing functionalities in iBEAT. We will develop novel techniques for infant cerebellar image tissue
segmentation, atlas building, surface reconstruction and parcellation, and enrich cerebrum-related functionalities
applicable for large-scale infant brain MRIs from diverse imaging sites, scanners, and protocols. We will feely
release our developed tools, atlases, and our processed dHCP/BCP/NDAR/HBCD data to the public.

title: Discovery Science Collaborative for CKDu
text:
The Discovery Science Collaborative for CKDu is a multi-PI application for the Renal Science Core for the
Chronic Kidney Diseases of UnceRtain Etiology (CKDu) in Agricultural Communities (CURE) Research
Consortium. The Renal Science Core consists of several Core components: Genomics, Pathology,
Transcriptomics, Biomarker / Proteomics, Physiology, and Bioinformatics / Data Integration. The RSC team is
uniquely poised to work within an NIDDK infrastructure with Field Epidemiology Sites, the Scientific Data
Coordinating Center, NIDDK leadership, HHEAR, and the External Oversight Committee to make significant
contributions to the CURE Consortium in discovery science and achieve the long-term goal of elucidating the
etiology, progression, and heterogeneity of CKDu in agricultural communities.

title: Ghrelin as Radiation Countermeasure: Mechanism of Its Action
text:
Individuals exposed to high doses of ionizing radiation can
develop deadly gastrointestinal acute radiation syndrome (GI-ARS) for which no specific treatment is yet
available. In this project, we will elucidate a novel neuroenteric mechanism through which human ghrelin
confers intestinal radioprotection, and leverage it to preclinically develop human ghrelin as a safe and effective
radiation mitigator for GI-ARS. These studies shall provide novel insights into the control of intestinal healing
by a new and effective treatment for victims of major radiation exposure.

title: Characterizing Breast and Cervical Cancer Burden Among Sexual Minority women
text: Women who identify as bisexual, lesbian, or queer have lower rates of breast and cervical cancer screening, but no large-scale data is available to understand the implications of these differences on cancer burden. In this project, we will better characterize breast and cervical cancer screening patterns by sexual orientation and simulate the expected burden of cancer given current knowledge on risk behaviors and screening patterns. This research will provide much needed estimates of stage-specific cancer incidence and mortality, as well as provide actionable insights on upstream determinants affecting cancer screening use and breast and cervical cancer risk by sexual orientation.

title: Neurometabolomics and Neuroproteomics Center on Cell-Cell Signaling
text:
Literally hundreds of thousands of chemically distinct molecules are present in every cell in the brain and can be
modified based on exposure to drugs of abuse, and yet the technologies to measure and elucidate this chemical
complexity are not broadly available. Our Center offers unparalleled measurement capabilities and analytical
support to a broad range of drug abuse and fundamental science projects, ensuring their success.

title: Molecular mechanisms of antibody-mediated immunotherapies
text:
Our studies focus on developing new and more effective immunotherapy strategies for treating cancer. The
proposed research will define pathways contributing to immune response within the tumor microenvironment
and test these findings using newly developed pre-clinical models. This work has the potential to significantly
advance cancer treatment by developing new treatment methods and by increasing the overall knowledge of the
biology of antibodies in the treatment of cancer.

title: MYC-alarmin axis as a novel therapeutic vulnerability in myelofibrosis
text:
Despite advances in our understanding of the underlying genetic abnormalities in myelofibrosis (MF) and the
development of JAK2 inhibitors, MF remains an aggressive chronic myeloid malignancy due to persistence of
JAK2-activating mutations in patients undergoing JAK2 inhibitor therapy, the emergence of drug resistance, and
a propensity for transformation to acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Thus, there is an urgent need to devise new
treatment strategies that target the molecular and genetic aberrations driving MF development and clonal
expansion, particularly in triple negative MF patients who lack mutations in the JAK2 kinase pathway. This R01
research program focuses on defining the roles of a new MYC-alarmin circuit that we have shown is sufficient to
provoke MF, and to preclinically assess the therapeutic potential of targeting this pathway to improve outcomes
in MF.

title: Single Cell Proteoform Profiling using Top-Down Mass Spectrometry
text:
Proteoforms play key roles in human health and disease and are effective
markers for differentiating cell types and heterogeneous cell populations. The proposed
research develops a suite of high-throughput technologies for enhanced proteoform profiling of
tissue-contained single cells particularly rare cells. This proposal will uncover novel molecular
signatures for tissue-resident innate immune cells and expand our knowledge on their roles to
furnish novel therapeutic strategies in relevant diseases.

title: Engineering a gut-on-chip model to study biomechanical forces on the enteric nervous system
text:
Functional gastrointestinal diseases, such as chronic idiopathic constipation, affect millions of Americans each
year and the vast majority of cases have no identifiable cause or effective treatment options. Neurons and glia
of the enteric nervous system (ENS) are important regulators of gastrointestinal function and are highly
vulnerable to mechanical stressors in the gut, such as stretch and shear stress, but our understanding of how
the ENS responds to biomechanical stress is limited. This R03 proposal will develop new technology and
methodology to determine the effect of biomechanical forces on enteric neurons and glia, ultimately enhancing
our understanding of neurointestinal physiology.

title: Circadian and homeostatic regulation of sleep in a diurnal model of Smith-Magenis Syndrome
text:
Smith-Magenis Syndrome (SMS) is a genetic disorder with cognitive, behavioral, circadian activity and sleep
disturbances, and sleep disturbances can worsen behavioral and cognitive symptoms. Leveraging here a
recently developed diurnal rodent, we will investigate the neural mechanisms underlying the sleep
disturbances in SMS. The results will contribute to better understanding of the neural mechanisms and to the
development of novel interventions for sleep problems in SMS and other neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: Investigating the role and therapeutic potential of the alpha5beta1 integrin in risk factors for COVID-19-associated cognitive impairment
text:
The interplay between vascular dementia (VaD) and COVID-19 morbidity, mortality, and post-COVID cognitive
decline is poorly understood and lacks effective treatments. Advancing age and other co-morbidities are
commonly associated with VaD and COVID-19 incidence and severity. Here we propose to investigate a novel
mechanism by which increased expression of integrin α5β1, a receptor that we have implicated in both VaD and
COVID-19, aggravates the pathophysiology of COVID-19 in the VaD-susceptible aged population using animal
and cell culture models.

title: Role of Cyr61/CCN1 in Mesenchymal Stem Cell Niche and Aging Bone
text:
Aging-related bone degeneration is a major healthcare challenge for America's growing population of
aging Veterans. Changes in bone mass and structure occur with age and are common in both women and men,
resulting in increased risk for debilitating pain, bone fracture, and delayed healing. With aging, resident stem
cells in bone lose their ability to maintain the tissue and bone degeneration takes place over time. My preliminary
results suggest that during aging, the level of a protein, Cyr61 (also known as CCN1), becomes depleted in
bone. The proposed research will investigate this protein and determine if it's required for normal function of
bone-specific stem cells and whether replenishing it during aging restores their function in bone. The results
gained from this study may provide a novel approach for reversing bone degeneration during aging or stimulating
bone repair after injury.

title: Nef-independent SERINC5 regulation
text:
Serine Incorporator 5 (SERINC5) is found at the plasma membrane of cells and is critical for the inhibition of
HIV-1 particle infectivity. Although the effect of Nef on SERINC5 is well described, it is currently unknown if
HIV-1 utilizes other strategies to counteract SERINC5. This proposal aims to elucidate strategies utilized by
HIV-1 to block the antiviral effect of SERINC5 that are currently unknown and have the potential of providing
novel therapeutic strategies targeting SERINC5-mediated restriction.

title: Extensible Open Source Zero-Footprint Web Viewer for Cancer Imaging Research
text:
The Open Health Imaging Foundation (OHIF) Viewer is a free, professional-grade, open source, web-based
medical imaging viewer and application framework that our team has created for the cancer community. OHIF
has been widely adopted by hundreds of imaging informatics projects in cancer research and beyond to
visualize and quantify disease within patients’ imaging exams. The current proposal will enhance and sustain
the platform to expand its image visualization and analysis capabilities, create user-friendly deployment
methods, and provide developer, end user, and regulatory support to help researchers better evaluate the
nature of cancer disease progression and response to treatment.

title: An LCMS-guided bioanalytical approach for rational natural product library design and optimization
text:
High-throughput screening of compound libraries is a fundamental starting point to drug development
efforts, and natural product libraries are one of the most valuable sources of novel bioactive molecules.
However, until now there have been few evidence-based rules for the rational design of natural product
libraries. This work is relevant to public health because it will demonstrate the utility of bioanalytical liquid
chromatography-mass spectrometry to addressing this biological need, and lead to accelerated drug
development in the long term.

title: Wake Forest NCORP Research Base
text: The Wake Forest NCORP Research Base develops and implements multi-site Cancer Control and Cancer Care Delivery (CCDR) clinical research studies in partnership with NCORP Sites to improve patient well-being and the quality of cancer care.

title: Project II - Leveraging artificial intelligence for integrative multiomics analysis of high-risk populations to understand the biologic etiology of pancreatic cancer
text: PROJECT SUMMARY – Project 2 Project 2 Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDA) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality in the United States, with rising incidence and death rates. Mortality rates vary across patient populations, and in those at the highest risk of developing PDA, mortality remains elevated even after accounting for established risk factors and socioeconomic measures. This pattern suggests a possible biological contribution. However, high-risk patient populations for which limited data are available have not been extensively investigated in publicly available genomic and clinical databases or in biorepositories, constraining the ability to conduct comprehensive analyses and develop refined precision therapeutic strategies. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) provide a powerful opportunity to bridge this gap by enabling large-scale, real-world data analyses. To address this gap, we will pursue three specific aims: In Aim 1, we will develop a natural language processing (NLP) model to extract structured and unstructured clinicopathologic data from clinical sources, facilitating standardized and scalable analyses. We will then apply this validated model to characterize the somatic mutational landscape of PDA in Hawai‘i and assess its impact on patient outcomes. In Aim 2, we will analyze clinically derived whole-exome and whole transcriptome sequencing data to evaluate subtype distribution, stromal composition, and stromal activation. Additionally, we will leverage AI-driven spatial transcriptomics to investigate tumor spatial organization, including tumor-stroma interactions, and their impact on patient outcomes. In Aim 3, we will generate patient derived organoids (PDOs) from metastatic PDA biopsies of patients from high-risk populations, addressing a critical lack of data in biorepositories. We will validate these PDOs through genomic, histopathological, and therapeutic sensitivity analyses and correlate findings with clinical outcomes to assess their translational potential. By integrating AI-driven data extraction, molecular characterization, and spatial transcriptomic analysis with patient-derived models, we aim to elucidate the molecular and spatial tumor features underlying PDA disparities and potentially identify novel predictive and prognostic biomarkers to improve patient outcomes.

title: Machine learning-enhanced cardiomyopathy prediction in childhood cancer survivors
text:
Over half of pediatric cancer survivors are at high risk for cardiomyopathy due to cardiotoxic exposures during
their cancer treatment. At-risk patients undergo serial echocardiographic screening, but echocardiography is
limited in its ability to detect subtle, potentially reversible cardiac changes before permanent damage is present.
This proposal will use an innovative combination of routinely collected clinical and echocardiographic data,
advanced machine learning techniques, and clinician stakeholder perspectives to optimize a machine learning
model for prediction of cardiomyopathy.

title: Ultrasensitive detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection
text:
Tuberculosis represents one of the most frequent causes of morbidity and mortality in humans worldwide.
Tuberculosis drug resistant infections are increasing throughout the world, making it critical that rapid
screening strategies are developed for therapeutics and other novel interventions. This project is geared
toward improvement and validation of groundbreaking imaging technologies that can be used to replace much
slower and inefficient conventional approaches to track bacterial viability, whole animal localization during
disease and speed development of novel therapeutics and vaccines.
